# 005 · An intended change, reviewed as a one-line contract diff

| **✓ Verified: all 36 cases match** | functional | none | feature, behaviour change intended | [`OrderLifecycle#decide`](../../examples/apps/boxoffice/ticketing-domain/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/boxoffice/ticketing/domain/OrderLifecycle.java) | [B8: Behavioural contracts](../../examples/tools/contracts/README.md) |

> Product asks for a clearer message when a customer cancels during payment. The developer changes the code and regenerates the contract, and the pull request shows exactly one changed outcome.

## The change

Change the rejection text for cancelling an order whose payment is in flight from 'try again shortly' to 'try again in a few seconds'.

**Before** ([`OrderLifecycle.java`](../../examples/apps/boxoffice/ticketing-domain/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/boxoffice/ticketing/domain/OrderLifecycle.java), line 51):

```java
            case PENDING_PAYMENT, CONFIRMED, DECLINED, REFUNDED -> unchanged("no refund outstanding");
        };
        case CancellationRequested _ -> switch (current) {
            case CONFIRMED -> transition(REFUND_PENDING, RELEASE_SEATS, REQUEST_REFUND);
            case REFUND_PENDING, REFUNDED -> unchanged("already cancelled");
            case PENDING_PAYMENT -> new Decision.Rejected("payment is in progress; try again shortly");
            case DECLINED -> new Decision.Rejected("the order was never paid");
        };
    };
}
```

**After:**

```java
            case PENDING_PAYMENT, CONFIRMED, DECLINED, REFUNDED -> unchanged("no refund outstanding");
        };
        case CancellationRequested _ -> switch (current) {
            case CONFIRMED -> transition(REFUND_PENDING, RELEASE_SEATS, REQUEST_REFUND);
            case REFUND_PENDING, REFUNDED -> unchanged("already cancelled");
            case PENDING_PAYMENT -> new Decision.Rejected("payment is in progress; try again in a few seconds");
            case DECLINED -> new Decision.Rejected("the order was never paid");
        };
    };
}
```

## What the verifier found

All 36 possible inputs give the same outcome as the contract.

Because the change was intended, the developer regenerated the contract. This diff is what the reviewer approves:

```diff
--- a/examples/apps/boxoffice/ticketing-domain/src/contract/OrderLifecycle.decide.contract
+++ b/examples/apps/boxoffice/ticketing-domain/src/contract/OrderLifecycle.decide.contract
@@ -8,7 +8,7 @@
 decide(PENDING_PAYMENT, PaymentCaptured[seatsStillHeld=true])  => Transition[next=CONFIRMED, effects=[SELL_SEATS]]
 decide(PENDING_PAYMENT, PaymentDeclined[])                     => Transition[next=DECLINED, effects=[RELEASE_SEATS]]
 decide(PENDING_PAYMENT, PaymentRefunded[])                     => Unchanged[reason="no refund outstanding"]
-decide(PENDING_PAYMENT, CancellationRequested[])               => Rejected[reason="payment is in progress; try again shortly"]
+decide(PENDING_PAYMENT, CancellationRequested[])               => Rejected[reason="payment is in progress; try again in a few seconds"]
 decide(PENDING_PAYMENT, null)                                  => throws NullPointerException
 decide(CONFIRMED, PaymentCaptured[seatsStillHeld=false])       => Unchanged[reason="payment already recorded"]
 decide(CONFIRMED, PaymentCaptured[seatsStillHeld=true])        => Unchanged[reason="payment already recorded"]
```

## Would the existing tests have caught it?

Every existing unit test passes, as it should (`:ticketing-domain:test`, run against the patched code).

## Why it matters

None, if the contract diff matches the intent. The point of the example is that the contract diff is how a reviewer confirms that the change did what was asked and nothing else, without reading the code.

## Why the verdict is right

The developer runs ./gradlew updateContracts, which rederives the contract from the new bytecode, and commits it with the code. The contract diff contains one line, for the one input whose outcome changed. Verification then passes. Had the edit also changed another case, that case would appear in the same diff.

## What to do

Review the contract diff against the ticket, then merge.
